schema:

bill_item(bill_no INT PK -> bill.bill_no, dish_code VARCHAR(5) PK -> dish.dish_code, qty INT)
dish(dish_code VARCHAR(5) PK, dish_name VARCHAR(40) ['Kacchi', ...], course VARCHAR(20) ['Main', 'Drink', 'Dessert', 'Starter'], price INT, calories INT)

staff(staff_no INT PK, full_name VARCHAR(40) ['Rafi', ...], duty VARCHAR(20) ['Manager', 'Waiter', 'Chef', 'Cleaner'], pay INT, joined DATE, outlet_no INT -> outlet.outlet_no, reports_to INT -> staff.staff_no)

answers.question: Show the dish name and price of every dish in the Main course, most expensive first.
answers.sql:
SELECT dish_name, price
FROM dish
WHERE course = 'Main'
ORDER BY price DESC;

answers.question: How many bills were paid with each payment mode? Show pay_mode and the number as Bill_Count.
Show the title of outlets that have never issued a bill.
Find the total money earned from each dish (price times quantity). Show dish_name and the amount as Revenue, highest first.
answers.sql:
SELECT d.dish_name, d.price * bi.qty AS Revenue
FROM dish d
JOIN bill_item bi ON d.dish_code = bi.dish_code
ORDER BY Revenue DESC;

answers.question: Show the dishes that were never ordered. Display dish_name.
List bill_no and bill_date for bills in 2024 on which no tip was recorded.
Show the total amount of each bill as Bill_Total with its bill_no, only for bills whose total exceeds 700.
answers.sql:
SELECT bill.bill_no, SUM(bill_item.qty * dish.price) AS Bill_Total
FROM bill
JOIN bill_item ON bill.bill_no = bill_item.bill_no
JOIN dish ON bill_item.dish_code = dish.dish_code
GROUP BY bill.bill_no
HAVING SUM(bill_item.qty * dish.price) > 700;

answers.question: Show the title of the outlet with the highest monthly rent.
Show the full_name of waiters who served Kacchi on at least one bill.
answers.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT b.full_name
FROM staff b
JOIN bill_item i ON b.staff_no = i.staff_no
JOIN dish d ON i.dish_code = d.dish_code
WHERE d.dish_name = 'Kacchi';

answers.question: Show the average pay per duty as Avg_Pay for duties having at least 2 people.
answers.sql:
SELECT c.duty, AVG(b.pay) AS Avg_Pay
FROM staff b
JOIN staff c ON b.reports_to = c.staff_no
GROUP BY c.duty
HAVING COUNT(b.staff_no) >= 2;
notes:
two drafts gave different results; the other draft was:
SELECT duty, AVG(pay) AS Avg_Pay
FROM staff
GROUP BY duty
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;

answers.question: Show the names of staff who have the same duty as Sumi, excluding Sumi.
answers.sql: SELECT full_name FROM staff WHERE duty = (SELECT duty FROM staff WHERE full_name = 'Sumi') AND full_name != 'Sumi';

answers.question: Create a view named Outlet_Income showing each outlet's title and its total income from dishes sold (price times quantity) as Income.
answers.sql:
CREATE VIEW Outlet_Income AS
SELECT a.title, SUM(l.price * bi.qty) AS Income
FROM outlet a
JOIN bill b ON a.outlet_no = b.outlet_no
JOIN bill_item bi ON b.bill_no = bi.bill_no
JOIN dish l ON bi.dish_code = l.dish_code
GROUP BY a.title;
